items.title: What Music Did Henry VIII Listen To?
items.description:
Music was a huge part of life at the Tudor Court. Henry VIII composed music and played with his wives. Elizabeth I was also a musician! 

People listened to both secular and sacred music in the 16th Century, but these styles were very different. global_silver_linings.title: Hyundai Partners with Healthy Seas to Turn Scourge ‘GhostNets’ into Floor Mats for Cars
global_silver_linings.snippet: Off the coast of Catalina Island for 15 years, the fishing vessel Midnight Hour has sat on the ocean floor—its sunken wreckage becoming a tangle of abandoned fishing nets, the kind that drift in the current while trapping debris—and marine life. Good News Network joined divers on the water for a mission to collect the […] The post Hyundai Partners with Healthy Seas to Turn Scourge ‘GhostNets’ into Floor Mats for Cars appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: Abandoned fishing nets are one of the ocean's most persistent threats to marine life, so turning them into car floor mats is a beautifully practical example of industry and conservation working together. It proves that harmful waste can be genuinely rerouted into something useful, not just talked about.

global_silver_linings.title: Soft decluttering: the low-pressure method for a tidier home
global_silver_linings.snippet: BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM You know the feeling: you walk toward the hall closet with good intentions, reach for the handle, and stop. The coats are in there, somewhere. So are the shoes that were trendy two seasons ago, a bag you haven’t opened in months, and something that might be an umbrella.
global_silver_linings.reason: A gentler approach to decluttering means more people can actually start — and that a tidier, calmer home is within reach without the stress of an all-or-nothing overhaul. Small, sustainable changes tend to stick in ways that dramatic ones don't.

discovery_articles.title: Spines of saber-toothed cats tell a tale of the doomed species
discovery_articles.snippet: Remains pulled from the La Brea Tar Pits revealed deformed vertebrae and rare tumors, possible signs of inbreeding among now-extinct saber-toothed cats.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The bones of these long-extinct predators aren't just fossils — they're a genetic confession, their twisted spines quietly recording the desperation of a population too small to save itself. There's something achingly human about reading a species' final chapter written in its own skeleton.

featured_read.title: How to Live a Miraculous Life
featured_read.snippet: Suppose we agree that we are here to love anyway — to love even though the work is almost unbearably difficult, even though we know that everything alive is dying, that everything beautiful is perishable, that everything we love will eventually be taken from us by one form of entropy or another, culminating with life itself. Suppose we agree that, as Rilke so passionately insisted, “for one human being to love another… is perhaps the most difficult of all our tasks, the ultimate, the last test and proof, the work for which all other work is but preparation.” This, then,… read article
featured_read.blurb: This essay sits with Rilke's most demanding idea — that love is not a gift we receive but a practice we must repeatedly, exhaustingly choose — and asks what it actually looks like to keep choosing it anyway. A quiet half-hour with this one might feel less like reading and more like being steadied.

garden_note.note: First light crept over the Zürichsee at 05:21 this morning, and by now the garden is already warm and humming — high summer in the Swiss Midtelland means dahlias nodding heavily with dew and the courgettes quietly becoming marrows overnight if you so much as blink. Step outside before the heat builds and enjoy the hour when everything still smells of earth rather than sun.

news.title: Vegan pho and Thai fishless cakes: Richard Makin’s southeast Asian-style tofu recipes
news.snippet: Fragrant, punchy vegan dishes that can be kept in the kept in the fridge or freezer for an easy midweek dinner Whether you love it or loathe it, tofu is one of the most versatile ingredients in any kitchen. For me, it’s the saviour of stressful dinner times, because it cooks in minutes, absorbs flavour like no other and packs a real nutritional punch. Here, it plays two very different roles: crisped until golden in a fragrant, spice-infused Vietnamese-style pho, and mashed to give body and bite to bold, punchy Thai-ish fishless cakes.
news.blurb: Richard Makin makes a compelling case for tofu with fragrant, freezer-friendly southeast Asian dishes that could genuinely convert even the most committed sceptic.

So I’ve spent the past few days washing, hulling, cutting and cooking my unexpected bounty. I’ve been making a number of...
recipe.blurb: A beautiful way to capture the sweetness of peak-season strawberries, David Lebovitz's homemade jam is a gentle, rewarding kitchen project that turns a lucky glut of fruit into something you'll be spreading on toast for weeks.

larder.seasonal_note: Zürich's Tuesday and Saturday markets at Bürkliplatz are brimming with Zürcher Unterland cherries right now — grab a bag of the dark, almost-jammy Kordia variety and, if you're feeling ambitious, fold them into a simple Kirschenkuchen before the afternoon heat sets in.

fern_data.greeting: The air at this hour has that particular high-summer weight — still almost cool, but with heat already coiled inside it, waiting. Enough to make Michael Stipe's new song feel exactly right, the Nebra Sky Disk feel ancient and urgent, and the question of how a species goes from apex predator to gone feel uncomfortably close to home.
